polite_rewrite: Hello Alex, I am sorry, but I need to cancel our meeting about the logo today. Something urgent has come up. Could we reschedule for tomorrow? I apologise for the inconvenience. I really appreciate your understanding.
explanation: A short apology plus a reschedule offer softens a late cancellation.

input: The client approved the newsletter milestone but the $800 payment still has not arrived. They messaged me this morning. The client runs a school.
polite_rewrite: Hi Ella, the newsletter milestone was approved and the $800 payment is still outstanding. Could you please confirm when it will be sent? I need to plan my schedule around it. I would appreciate a reply this week.
explanation: Clear facts plus a reason for the deadline make firmness polite.

input: The client is a nonprofit and asked for a lower rate on the booking system. I can offer 10 percent off. We have been talking over phone. The budget was agreed last Friday.
polite_rewrite: Hi Ryan! I love what your nonprofit does. I can offer a 10 percent discount on the booking system. The fee would be $250 instead of the usual rate. I hope that helps.
explanation: A small nonprofit discount shows goodwill while keeping most of the fee.

input: I need to follow up on an unpaid invoice for the presentation for the third time. The budget was agreed two days ago. It is for their new restaurant.
polite_rewrite: Hi Ryan, this is my third follow-up on the overdue invoice for the presentation. I understand things get busy, but I do need a payment date this week. Could you confirm one by Friday?
explanation: Counting the follow-ups calmly justifies asking for a firm date.

input: I want to check in with a client I have not heard from in three months about the blog setup. The budget was agreed on Monday. We have been talking over LinkedIn.
polite_rewrite: Hi Priya! it has been a while! I hope you are doing well. I wanted to check in and see how the blog setup is performing. If you need any updates, I am here.
explanation: A friendly check-in after months keeps the relationship alive.

input: I need to introduce myself to a client team I have never met for the chatbot. The client runs a fashion brand. They messaged me this morning.
polite_rewrite: Hello everyone, thank you for having me. I am the designer working on your new chatbot. I look forward to collaborating with you all over the coming weeks.
explanation: A brief team introduction establishes the role and the timeline.

input: Client asked me to do their competitor research for free as a favour alongside the explainer video. They messaged me on Monday.
polite_rewrite: Hi Grace, that kind of research usually takes me a full day. I could look at it as a small separate project if it would help. What do you think?
explanation: Mentioning the time involved hints at the cost without a blunt refusal.

input: The client loves the booking system work and left great feedback. I want to thank them warmly. It is for their new fashion brand. They replied last week.
polite_rewrite: Hey Aisha, thank you so much for the wonderful feedback on the booking system! It means a lot to hear that. I really enjoyed working on this project with you.
explanation: Warm gratitude for praise strengthens the relationship.

input: how do I greet a new client professionally in my first email about the logo? We usually talk over LinkedIn. They replied yesterday.
polite_rewrite: Hey Lily, thank you for reaching out about the logo. I appreciate the opportunity to work with you. Please find my portfolio attached, and I look forward to discussing your project. Really appreciate it!
explanation: A warm greeting with a portfolio attachment sets a professional first impression.
